article.title: An ideal city

items.sentence_raw: The word 'genius' is universally associated with the name of Leonardo da Vinci.
A true Renaissance man, he embodied scientific spirit, artistic talent and humanist sensibilities.
Five hundred years have passed since Leonardo died in his home at Château du Clos Lucé, outside Tours, France.
Yet far from fading into insignificance, his thinking has carried down the centuries and still surprises today.

The Renaissance marked the transition from the 15th century to modernity and took place after the spread of the plague in the 14th century, which caused a global crisis resulting in some 200 million deaths across Europe and Asia.
Today, the world is on the cusp of a climate crisis, which is predicted to cause widespread displacement, extinctions and death, if left unaddressed.
Then, as now, radical solutions were called for to revolutionise the way people lived and safeguard humanity against catastrophe.
items.explain: Q29: The passage says *'Then, as now, radical solutions were called for to revolutionise the way people lived and safeguard humanity against catastrophe'*. Here, **'then'** refers to Renaissance times and **'now'** refers to today — this directly compares the challenges. So the answer is **TRUE**.

items.sentence_raw: Around 1486 - after a pestilence that killed half the population in Milan, Italy - Leonardo turned his thoughts to urban planning problems.
Following a typical Renaissance trend, he began to work on an 'ideal city' project, which - due to its excessive costs - would remain unfulfilled.
items.explain: Q30: The passage says Leonardo's ideal city project *'would remain unfulfilled'* — **'unfulfilled'** means it was **not** built. The question says it **'was constructed'**, which is the opposite. So the answer is **FALSE**.

items.sentence_raw: Yet given that unsustainable urban models are a key cause of global climate change today, it's only natural to wonder how Leonardo might have changed the shape of modern cities.
items.explain: Q31: The passage says *'unsustainable urban models are a key cause of global climate change today'*. **'Unsustainable urban models'** is another way of saying **'poor town planning'**, and **'a key cause'** means it is a **'major contributor'**. So the answer is **TRUE**.

items.sentence_raw: Although the Renaissance is renowned as an era of incredible progress in art and architecture, it is rarely noted that the 15th century also marked the birth of urbanism as a true academic discipline.

The rigour and method behind the conscious conception of a city had been largely missing in Western thought until the moment when prominent Renaissance men pushed forward large-scale urban projects in Italy, such as the reconfiguration of the town of Pienza and the expansion of the city of Ferrara.
These works surely inspired Leonardo's decision to rethink the design of medieval cities, with their winding and overcrowded streets and with houses piled against one another.
It is not easy to identify a coordinated vision of Leonardo's ideal city because of his disordered way of working with notes and sketches.
items.explain: Q33: The passage says it is hard to identify his vision because of his *'disordered way of working with notes and sketches'*. **'Disordered'** means messy and not organised — the opposite of **'neat, organised'**. So the answer is **FALSE**.

items.sentence_raw: But from the largest collection of Leonardo's papers ever assembled, a series of innovative thoughts can be reconstructed regarding the foundation of a new city along the Ticino River, which runs from Switzerland into Italy and is 248 kilometres long.
He designed the city for the easy transport of goods and clean urban spaces, and he wanted a comfortable and spacious city, with well-ordered streets and architecture.
items.explain: Q34: The passage says Leonardo designed the city for the *'easy transport of goods'*. The question asks for better **'transport'** for trade — **'goods'** are items for trade. So the answer is **transport**.

items.sentence_raw: He recommended 'high, strong walls', with 'towers and battlements of all necessary and pleasant beauty'.
His plans for a modern and 'rational' city were consistent with Renaissance ideals.
But, in keeping with his personality, Leonardo included several innovations in his urban design.
Leonardo wanted the city to be built on several levels, linked with vertical outdoor staircases.
items.explain: Q35: The passage says the city levels were *'linked with vertical outdoor staircases'*. The question describes these as features *'on the exterior of a building'* — **'outdoor'** means exterior. So the answer is **staircases**.

items.sentence_raw: This design can be seen in some of today's high-rise buildings but was unconventional at the time.
Indeed, this idea of taking full advantage of the interior spaces wasn't implemented until the 1920s and 1930s, with the birth of the Modernist movement.
While in the upper layers of the city, people could walk undisturbed between elegant palaces and streets, the lower layer was the place for services, trade, transport and industry.
But the true originality of Leonardo's vision was its fusion of architecture and engineering.
items.explain: Q36: The passage says the true originality was the *'fusion of architecture and engineering'*. The question says his expertise in **'engineering'** was evident in the canal plans — this matches the second part of that fusion. So the answer is **engineering**.

items.sentence_raw: Leonardo designed extensive hydraulic plants to create artificial canals throughout the city.
The canals, regulated by clocks and basins, were supposed to make it easier for boats to navigate inland.

Leonardo also thought that the width of the streets ought to match the average height of the adjacent houses: a rule still followed in many contemporary cities across Italy, to allow access to sun and reduce the risk of damage from earthquakes.
items.explain: Q37: The passage says matching house height to street width is a *'rule still followed in many contemporary cities across Italy'*. The question says the design of many Italian cities today follows this **'rule'**. So the answer is **rule**.

items.sentence_raw: Although some of these features existed in Roman cities, before Leonardo's drawings there had never been a multi-level, compact modern city which was thoroughly technically conceived.
items.explain: Q38: The passage says *'some of these features existed in Roman cities'*. The question asks which earlier times had similar aspects — **'Roman'** times directly matches. So the answer is **Roman**.

items.sentence_raw: Indeed, it wasn't until the 19th century that some of his ideas were applied.

For example, the subdivision of the city by function - with services and infrastructures located in the lower levels and wide and well-ventilated boulevards and walkways above for residents - is an idea that can be found in Georges-Eugène Haussmann's renovation of Paris under Emperor Napoleon III between 1853 and 1870.
items.explain: Q39: The passage gives the example of *'Georges-Eugène Haussmann's renovation of Paris'* in the 19th century. The question asks for a city redesigned in the 19th century as Leonardo envisaged — that city is **Paris**. So the answer is **Paris**.

items.sentence_raw: Today, Leonardo's ideas are not simply valid, they actually suggest a way forward for urban planning.

Many scholars think that the compact city, built upwards instead of outwards, integrated with nature (especially water systems), with efficient transport infrastructure, could help modern cities become more efficient and sustainable.
items.explain: Q40: The passage says the compact city is *'built upwards instead of outwards'*. The question says building **'outwards'** is no longer the best approach — **'instead of'** shows that **'outwards'** is the old, less good way. So the answer is **outwards**.

items.sentence_raw: This is yet another reason why Leonardo was aligned so closely with modern urban planning and centuries ahead of his time.

subtitles: Leonardo da Vinci's ideal city was centuries ahead of its time

orphan_explain_map.27: Q27: The passage says Leonardo died 500 years ago, but it never mentions when people **first** called him a genius. The word *'genius'* is linked to his name, but there is no date for the **first** use. ***NOT GIVEN is not the same as FALSE*** — the information is simply missing, so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
orphan_explain_map.28: Q28: The passage says the plague caused *'some 200 million deaths'*, but for the climate crisis it only predicts *'widespread displacement, extinctions and death'* without a number. There is no comparison of total deaths between the two events. ***Do not guess from general knowledge*** — since the passage does not compare the numbers, the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
orphan_explain_map.32: Q32: The passage mentions the reconfiguration of Pienza and expansion of Ferrara, but it only says these works *'inspired'* Leonardo. It never mentions whether **local people** fought against these changes. ***NOT GIVEN is not the same as FALSE*** — the information about local opposition is missing, so the answer is **NOT GIVEN**.
